thread:
Alex: quick question about per-route quota semantics during fallback — we ran into a weird case in staging where requests to /v1/generate (route A) get auto-routed to model-small (route B) when hot GPU pools are full. Do we emit a 429 for A, for B, or only if both are exhausted?

Priya: my understanding: runtime should only 429 if no compatible fallback can serve within the latency/cost policy. If fallback is used successfully, client should get a 200 from the served route. But we need clear headers so clients can reason about quotas/billing.

Sam: agree we should be explicit in headers. Backcompat requirement: new headers must be additive and optional. SDKs should ignore unknown headers.

Miko: proposal for minimal header surface (additive):
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
RateLimit-Limit: 100
RateLimit-Remaining: 0
RateLimit-Reset: 1670000000
RateLimit-Bucket: 0a3f
RateLimit-Served-Route: model-small
Retry-After: 15
```
Notes: RateLimit-Served-Route only present when we routed to a different bucket/route than requested. If original route was blocked and we served fallback, we include both Route headers (see below).

Alex: follow-up: should the runtime decrement the original route's bucket when it falls back? Two camps:
- charge original route (keeps client-side counters consistent for request intent)
- charge served route (matches actual resource consumption and billing)
This matters for SDKs doing client-side token accounting.

Priya: lean toward charging the served route. Otherwise customers will underpay/overpay confusion when observability shows consumption on served pool. But include headers to signal the original request route so SDKs can decide. e.g. `RateLimit-Request-Route: /v1/generate` and `RateLimit-Served-Route: model-small`.

Jordi: small ops ask: can RateLimit-Bucket be stable at the route level (not pod instance) so clients/cache layers can key by bucket? If bucket is ephemeral per process it defeats caching.

Sam: yes make bucket stable per logical quota group (route + customer tier). Runtime: don't rotate bucket IDs frequently. We'll add that to the ticket. :thumbsup:

Miko: another runtime nuance — streaming vs non-streaming behavior. For streaming connections we currently try to avoid mid-stream 429s (we prefer graceful close + final error chunk). Should SDKs treat a 429 received mid-stream the same as a terminal error? My vote: yes, treat as terminal and surface to user.

Alex: also need clarity on Retry-After semantics — should it be seconds (int) or HTTP-date? We have mixed usage across services. SDKs prefer seconds for simple backoff.

Sam: standardize on seconds (integer) for Retry-After and keep HTTP-date optional. Add to contract doc.

RateLimiterBot: created ticket RL-342: "per-route fallback quota semantics + header contract" and assigned to eng-runtime.

Alex: can eng-runtime do a quick sanity check on these header names and the decrementing model? If we standardize: `RateLimit-Request-Route`, `RateLimit-Served-Route`, `RateLimit-Bucket`, `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset`, `Retry-After`. Also confirm whether we should emit a `RateLimit-Fallback` boolean header when fallback occurred.

Sam: will review, but initial thumbs-up. If eng-runtime agrees we'll update the API contract doc and SDKs.

Priya: thanks. If anyone wants I can draft a one-pager with examples (200 vs 429 vs fallback) — ping @Sam and @Miko for review.

Alex: thanks all — pinging here because this affects client SDKs and the billing/observability dashboards.

Miko: small nit: include an example for streaming close semantics in the one-pager.

Sam: noted. I'll mark RL-342 as blocker for the next SDK patch.
